limitations: Small curated synthetic corpus with vocabulary overlap, not held-out real-world retrieval or end-to-end answer quality.
Recall@k and MRR are macro-averages over queries with accessible relevant chunks. No-accessible-evidence queries are excluded, not scored as perfect.
Nearest-neighbor retrieval always returns candidates when available; this benchmark does not measure abstention or add a relevance threshold.
Only chunk ids, source hashes and distances are recorded, not retrieved text.
Exploratory comparison on already inspected, tiny agent-curated synthetic corpora; not held-out quality, end-to-end answer quality or grounds for production adoption.
BM25 uses existing hashing tokenization, unique query terms, fixed k1=1.2 and b=0.75; no parameter tuning, synonyms, stemming changes or score threshold.
Both rankers use one repeatable-read, read-only snapshot. BM25 scores all permitted chunks with statistics computed only from that principal's catalog.
BM25 scores (larger is better) are not vector distances (smaller is better). Zero-overlap candidates are retained, so this does not measure abstention.
Catalog hashes cover sorted permitted chunk ids/source hashes, not retrieved text. No model calls, downloads, writes, production ranking or judgment changes.
Full-catalog Python scoring is an experiment for the small seed, not a scalable production implementation or a latency benchmark.
